evidence_claims.claim: Fuses and ordinary breakers handle overcurrent, not every shock/arc hazard

supports.location: p.1 AFCI vs GFCI, ordinary protection limitations

evidence_claims.limitations: Actual combination devices may offer more than one function.

evidence_claims.claim: GFCI/RCD measures imbalance through monitored load conductors
evidence_claims.limitations: Exact sensing type, wiring and response time require full product docs.

evidence_claims.claim: Balanced line-neutral body contact may evade residual detection
evidence_claims.limitations: Independent mechanism-specific corroboration not reviewed; safety-critical limitation remains true under specified balance hypothesis.

evidence_claims.claim: RCD is supplemental; it cannot prevent every electric shock
evidence_claims.limitations: No recommendation to work energized or deliberate testing by shock.

evidence_claims.claim: IEC RCCB scope excludes integral overcurrent protection
evidence_claims.limitations: Full normative text not inspected; application-specific design pending.

evidence_claims.claim: UL 943 scope refers to specified Class A personnel GFCIs
evidence_claims.limitations: Scope only; full test requirements and individual certification not checked.

evidence_claims.claim: AFCI addresses some arcing fire mechanisms distinct from GFCI
evidence_claims.limitations: Device performance conditional and intended application limited.

supports.location: §1.3 explicitly says not intended to detect glowing connections

evidence_claims.limitations: Direct public scope statement; full standard not inspected; not a promise of behavior of every product.

evidence_claims.claim: UL 1449 covers designated transient surge limiting devices
evidence_claims.limitations: Publisher scope only; no actual SPD selection/voltage claim verified.

evidence_claims.claim: Test button does not verify entire installation or safe absence of voltage
evidence_claims.limitations: Product instructions and qualified testing required; test button alone not safe-work verification.

evidence_claims.claim: Code adoption, panel compatibility and listing are separate requirements
evidence_claims.limitations: Occupational rule does not prove private-household permission; exact local adopted codes and product list required.

evidence_claims.claim: A tripping device is a symptom not an assured diagnosis
evidence_claims.limitations: Specific trip cause must be investigated by competent personnel; not DIY diagnostics.

evidence_claims.claim: Illustrative 8.00 vs 7.98 ampere residual equals 20 mA
evidence_claims.limitations: Arithmetic only: no trip-time or waveform prediction and no intentional fault test.

evidence_review.scope: claim-level checks of public explanations, regulatory provisions, published standards scope and selected engineering material; original calculations cross-checked
evidence_review.claim_level_corroboration: Partial; individual claim entries identify evidence and gaps

description: Addresses topics from the lecture, including "Begin with an ordinary fuse or circuit breaker"; "Residual current is a difference, not a label on a wire"; and "What ground fault does not mean".
